usage.reason: The provided documentation describes no per-user last-active field, audit/activity log, or per-user usage report for the Resource Management API.

evidence.quote: you can specify your API token as a query parameter named `auth`, or as an HTTP header with the same name.
If you have the Resourcing Administrator role, you can access your organization's token in the Resource Management application.

assumptions: The source pages mix three products (Smartsheet Resource Management, core Smartsheet, Brandfolder). I wrote the manifest for Resource Management, because it is the only one whose page documents a user list endpoint (GET /users).
The documentation does not show what the /users response looks like. The records path ("data") and the field names (id, email, display_name) are guesses and must be checked against a real response.
No status, role, user type, last-active or created-at fields could be confirmed, so they are left empty. Deactivated or archived people may or may not be returned by the list.
Page numbering is assumed to start at 1 (the example uses page=3, but the first page is not stated).

The base URL is the US region. EU (api.rm.smartsheet.eu), AU (api.rm.smartsheet.au) and Gov (app.smartsheetgov.com/2.0/rm/api/v1, which also needs a Smartsheet bearer token) use different hosts and are not covered.
The token belongs to the organization and is shown to users with the Resourcing Administrator role. It is not tied to one person, but it is unclear whether it survives that admin leaving.
Usage is unavailable: no last-active field, activity log or per-user report is documented for Resource Management.
The documentation does not state rate limits, so rate limit settings are left empty. Errors use standard HTTP status codes, so no error envelope is set.
